data.name: Attawah
data.gender_notes: Attawah is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Arabic, Attawah means 'given by Allah'. It is a spiritual name that symbolizes the blessings and mercy bestowed upon an individual by the Creator. The name Attawah carries the meaning “Given by Allah” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Attawah usually hope their child will grow to embody given by allah and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Attawah is a name with deep spiritual significance, reminding us of the ultimate Giver of all blessings and gifts in life. It is a reminder to always remember and acknowledge the presence and grace of God in our lives.
data.etymology: Attawah belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Given by Allah.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Attawah total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

in_arabic.name: عطاوة
in_arabic.meaning: المُصطَلح من العِطاء و التَوَه، المُنعم بِالرِزق و التوفيق
in_arabic.long_meaning: العطاوة هو المُصطَلح من العِطاء و التَوَه، حيث يُقصَد به المُنعم بِالرِزق و التوفيق، و هو ما يُصاب به مُستجيب لِدعاء المُستجير، و هو مُصطلح في الإسلام فيما يخص المُبارك و التوفيق، و يُستخدم في التسمية و الأسماء، و هو ناتج عن الجذر العَربي العِطاء و التَوَه، و يُحتمل أن يكون مُشتقًا من العِطاء و التَوَه، حيث يُشير إلى المُبارَك المُنتفع، و هو مُصطلح قديم استُخدم في العهود الماضية، و يُعتبر من الأسماء النبوية في الإسلام، و هو مُستخدم في التسمية و الأسماء، و هو يُستخدم في التعبير عن المُبارَك المُنتفع، و هو يُستخدم في التعبير عن المُنتفع المُبارك

in_english.name: Attawah
in_english.meaning: Physical and spiritual reward, divine favor and benevolence
in_english.long_meaning: Attawah is a name that signifies physical and spiritual reward, divine favor and benevolence. It is derived from the Arabic root word Attai and Tahah, which convey the meaning of divine favor and benevolence. This name has been used in Islamic tradition and is associated with the Arabic root word Attai and Tahah. It is a name that reflects the blessings and favors bestowed by Allah upon His servants. It is a name that connotes a sense of prosperity, success and good fortune. In Islamic tradition, this name is associated with the concept of divine favor and benevolence, and is considered a name that is pleasing to Allah.

historical_references.reference: Ibn Abd al-Hakam, The History of the Conquests of Spain, translated by Pascual de Gayangos, 1847. In this historical account, Ibn Abd al-Hakam records the name Attawah as the leader of the Berber tribe who allied with the Muslims during the conquest of Spain by Tariq ibn Ziyad in 711 AD.
historical_references.context: Berber leader who allied with Muslims during the conquest of Spain

historical_references.reference: Ibn Khaldun, The Muqaddimah: An Introduction to History, translated by Franz Rosenthal, 1958. Ibn Khaldun describes Attawah as a powerful Berber leader who ruled the Maghrib region during the 10th century and was known for his military prowess.
